decision: Promising private controller, not enabled: six Excel pairs improve; Word CPU and large RAM controls show small regressions. Next remove native exit overhead by moving controller entry outside generated blocks.
design: Replace recursive continueNative resolver with one bounded loop. It clears transient CPU chain budget before invoking child functions, so child exits return directly to the controller without nested resolver frames. Guards, early exits, aggregate instruction accounting and logical dispatch calendar remain checked.
sourceIdentity: Frozen native-batch source identified by native-batching-2026-10-26.json; same O3 build.

limits: Ratios are baseline/candidate; above one favors candidate. Shared host, six Office pairs and three RAM pairs per dispatch mode. No formal confidence interval.
Word response is neutral but CPU median slightly regresses. Large RAM batched controls regress; no default acceptance claim.
Instrumented recursive-bridge adoption counts belong to that prior prototype, not a measured iterative-controller adoption count.
No fresh OS installer acceptance repeated for this private executable. Existing external snapshots reused; expected task pixels pass and successful children removed.
No claim of another 2x useful-work improvement.
